subject: Question: SKU packaging multipliers, minimums, and per-token rounding
messages:
From: Maya Patel <maya.patel@lumenretail.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Lumen Retail <procurement@lumenretail.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Clarify billing for pipelines + context minimums

Hi Sergio,

Quick question from procurement as we lock down the SOW: when we run the recommendation pipeline we described (embedding -> retrieval -> 2-model ensemble for ranking + final answer), how are tokens billed across those steps? Specifically:

- Do we get charged per-token for each model invocation in the pipeline (so the same user prompt could be counted multiple times)?
- If we enable long-context sessions for chat (30k window) do minimums apply per-call or per-conversation? Our usage includes many short calls but large indexed context.
- What's the rounding behavior -- are we rounding up per-model, per-call, or per-invoice line item? We want to understand how the proposed discount interacts with minimum billing bands.

Procurement asked that we get a simple worked example we can include in the contract exhibit. Can you send something concise?

Thanks,
Maya
Maya Patel, Director of ML Platform
Lumen Retail

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Maya Patel <maya.patel@lumenretail.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify billing for pipelines + context minimums

Hi Maya — thanks for the clear asks. I put together a short explainer and will attach a worked example (Excel) for the exhibit. High level answers first: 

1) Per-model invocation: yes, we bill tokens consumed by each model invocation. So if the prompt is passed to Model A (embedding prep) and then Model B (ranker) and Model C (answering), each model's request/response tokens are counted independently.

2) Minimums: minimum billing (session or per-call floors) is applied based on the SKU in the contract. For our recommended "conversation" SKU with long-context windows (30k), minimums are typically evaluated per active session (per-session floor). That said, for high-volume short calls we can map to a per-call SKU to avoid amplifying minimums across micro-invocations.

3) Rounding: token granularity is applied at the request level (we round up to the nearest billing quantum per request per SKU) and invoice lines aggregate those rounded units. Practically that means small repeated invocations can trigger multiple small rounds unless we configure prefix/KV caching and batching which reduces duplicate billing.

I'm looping in Kimberly and Karthik to confirm the exact math for the discount carve-out and to provide the worked example you requested. I'll attach a short MAP + proposed pricing table in my next note.

Best,
Sergio
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify billing for pipelines + context minimums

Sergio / Kimberly — quick math check before we send to Maya: attached sample does three things 
- shows per-invocation token counts for the three-model pipeline,
- shows the effect of per-request rounding (we assume 50-token quantum for the per-token SKU in the workbook),
- shows how the 15% discount on billable tokens applies but not to committed-minimum credits.

Notes: if the customer takes our conversation SKU (session-based) we can apply a session minimum instead of per-call minimums; the spreadsheet includes a side-by-side for both paths. One call-out: the current discount in the PSA (15%) was intended to apply to billable tokens after rounding but before bundling credits are consumed; if Procurement wants the discount applied to the committed-minimum portion we need a formal concession approval (I can draft a brief memo).

I'll also include a worked example where KV cache prevents the ranking model from rerunning on the same prefix (saves ~30% of billable tokens on average).

Karthik
Senior Pricing Analyst

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Maya Patel <maya.patel@lumenretail.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-05T08:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify billing for pipelines + context minimums

Maya — attaching the worked example and a brief MAP. Highlights from the spreadsheet: 

- Example scenario: 1 user prompt -> Embedding prep (Model E) consumes 80 tokens, Retrieval engine adds 1,200 tokens to the model context, Ranker (Model R) consumes 320 tokens, Final answer (Model F) consumes 420 response tokens (including prompt).
- Per-invocation billing (no caching): total billed tokens = 80 + 320 + 420 = 820 tokens (note: retrieval context is included in prompt size for Model F but only counted once when sent to Model F; retrieval engine charges on its own call).
- Rounding (50-token quantum): 820 -> each model request rounded up per-invocation can add ~<50 tokens depending on segmentation; in the workbook we show a +110-token overhead across the three calls in this example.
- With caching/batching (recommended): ranker not invoked for cached prefixes -> reduce billed tokens to ~580 in the sample.

I called out two contract options: 
A) Conversation SKU (session minimum 50k tokens/month): we attach commit credits and apply discount to billable overage. Committed credits consume usage first (no discount on credits).
B) Per-call token SKU: 50-token quantum, discount applies to billable tokens post-rounding; no session minimum but higher per-token list price.

Please review the attached workbook. If Procurement needs the exhibit language, I can produce a short table and a one-paragraph explanation suitable for inclusion in Appendix A.

Regards,
Sergio

Attachments: 20261105-proposed_pricing_table.xlsx, 20261105-mutual_action_plan.pdf

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-05T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify billing for pipelines + context minimums

+1 to Karthik's note. A couple practical points for the contract exhibit: 

- Rounding language: propose "tokens rounded up to the nearest 50-token billing quantum per request". That keeps legal language simple and aligns with our billing engine.
- Discount carve-out: default posture is discount applies to billable tokens after rounding and after credits are consumed. If Lumen requests discount on committed credits, that is negotiable but requires Revenue approval and will reduce the effective list discount.
- Billing examples: I recommend two line items in the exhibit — one showing the per-call path (no commit) and one the session/commit path with example monthly amortization of credits. Procurement likes explicit numbers; use the numbers Sergio attached.

If we need to change the quantum (50 -> 100) for simplicity in the SOW, note it changes the rounding overhead materially; include both in the exhibit so Procurement can choose.

Kimberly
Director, Revenue Operations

Also happy to create the appendix language for Appendix A.

If Procurement is comfortable, we can sign the MAP and attach the exhibit with the per-call and per-session worked examples and the chosen quantum. Otherwise, we can mark the quantum as TBD and include both options in the SOW.

Tessa Morgan
